artworld-01-c1.text: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (2025). 50 Works 50 Weeks: Katsushika Hokusai’s “The Great Wave off Kanagawa”. Unframed (LACMA).
artworld-01-c1.quote: This print is part of his much celebrated series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, which the artist began in 1830 when he was 70 years old.
artworld-01-c1.claim: It comes from a series that Hokusai began in 1830, when he was 70 years old

artworld-01-c1.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (E.4823-1916). V&A Explore the Collections.
artworld-01-c1.quote: This print is from Hokusai's ground-breaking series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the first to exist exclusively of large-format prints of landscapes.
artworld-01-c1.claim: It was the first series made up entirely of large-format landscape prints.

artworld-01-c1.text: Dominik Havsteen-Franklin (2026). Hokusai’s Great Wave is one of 46 prints of Mount Fuji – seeing them together changes everything. The Conversation.
artworld-01-c1.quote: Dulwich Picture Gallery is showing all of Hokusai’s 36 Views of Mount Fuji, including ten added after the series became popular.
artworld-01-c1.claim: because ten more were added after the series became popular

artworld-01-c2.text: Hugh Davies (2017). Friday essay: from the Great Wave to Starry Night, how a blue pigment changed the world. The Conversation.
artworld-01-c2.quote: But although extremely popular in mainstream society, these woodblock prints were seen as vulgar by the Japanese literati and beneath consideration for artistic merit.
artworld-01-c2.claim: To the scholarly elite, these prints were vulgar.

artworld-01-c2.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. Japanese woodblock prints (ukiyo-e). Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-01-c2.quote: Normally, copyists' drawings would be destroyed in the production of the key-block.
artworld-01-c2.claim: The copy was destroyed in the process, which is why such drawings rarely survive.

artworld-01-c2.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. Japanese woodblock prints (ukiyo-e). Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-01-c2.quote: In the 1740s, additional woodblocks were used to print the colours pink and green, but it wasn't until 1765 that the technique of using multiple colour woodblocks was perfected.
artworld-01-c2.claim: Full-colour printing from many blocks was perfected in 1765

artworld-01-c3.text: Hugh Davies (2017). Friday essay: from the Great Wave to Starry Night, how a blue pigment changed the world. The Conversation.
artworld-01-c3.quote: In the early 1800s, a Guangzhou entrepreneur deciphered the recipe and began manufacturing the pigment in China at a much lower cost.
artworld-01-c3.claim: By the early 1800s a manufacturer in Guangzhou, China, was making it more cheaply

artworld-01-c3.text: Hugh Davies (2017). Friday essay: from the Great Wave to Starry Night, how a blue pigment changed the world. The Conversation.
artworld-01-c3.quote: Claude Monet was so seduced by the “Japonism” aesthetic he acquired 250 Japanese prints, including 23 by Hokusai.
artworld-01-c3.claim: Claude Monet acquired 250 Japanese prints, 23 of them by Hokusai.

artworld-01-c3.text: Van Gogh Museum. Utagawa Hiroshige. Van Gogh Museum: Japanese prints.
artworld-01-c3.quote: There are signs of Hiroshige’s prints being used in Van Gogh’s studio, such as paint stains and pinpricks, so it is clear that the prints directly inspired Van Gogh’s work.
artworld-01-c3.claim: The prints he owned carry pinpricks and paint stains, the physical traces of being pinned up in a working studio.

artworld-02-c1.text: National Palace Museum (2015). Exemplar of Heritage: Fan Kuan and His Influence in Chinese Painting. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c1.quote: Among landscape paintings with Fan Kuan’s name, “Travelers Among Mountains and Streams” in the National Palace Museum is the one most highly regarded and widely accepted as from his hand.
artworld-02-c1.claim: Of all the paintings that carry Fan Kuan's name, it is the one most widely accepted as really from his hand.

artworld-02-c1.text: National Palace Museum (2015). Exemplar of Heritage: Fan Kuan and His Influence in Chinese Painting. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c1.quote: And hidden among the trees to the lower right side of this large scroll are two characters for Fan Kuan’s name that represent his signature.
artworld-02-c1.claim: Hidden in the foliage are two characters: Fan Kuan's signature.

artworld-02-c1.text: National Palace Museum (2015). Exemplar of Heritage: Fan Kuan and His Influence in Chinese Painting (The Heritage of Travelers Among Mountains and Streams). National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c1.quote: Xuanhe Painting Manual, a catalogue of the imperial collection of painting under the Song emperor Huizong (r. 1100-1125), records 58 works by Fan Kuan but none with the title “Travelers Among Mountains and Streams.”
artworld-02-c1.claim: lists 58 paintings by Fan Kuan, and none has this name

artworld-02-c2.text: National Palace Museum (2017). The Making of a National Treasure: Select Masterpieces of Painting and Calligraphy in the Museum Collection. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c2.quote: No originals by Wang survive today, but this work as a faithful tracing copy from the Tang dynasty (608-907) serves as one of the most important pieces of visual evidence for later generations to understand his calligraphy.
artworld-02-c2.claim: No original by Wang Xizhi survives.

artworld-02-c2.text: National Palace Museum (2025). An Assembly for the Ages: The Legend of the Northern Song Elegant Gathering in the Western Garden. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c2.quote: The brushwork also does not feature the steady, condensed quality of Su Shi's brushstrokes.
artworld-02-c2.claim: Above all, it lacks the steady, condensed quality of Su Shi's own strokes.

artworld-02-c3.text: Taipei Times (2011). Classic Chinese painting ‘reunited’ after 400 years. Taipei Times.
artworld-02-c3.quote: It was almost destroyed in 1650 when collector Wu Hongyu (吳洪裕) attempted to burn the painting, but it was fortunately saved by a family member.
artworld-02-c3.claim: In 1650 the dying collector Wu Hongyu tried to have it burned.

artworld-02-c3.text: National Palace Museum (2025). Enduring Legacy: A Centennial Celebration of the National Palace Museum. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c3.quote: In the following year, when the Master Wuyong Scroll arrived, he thought of it as a forged copy.
artworld-02-c3.claim: When the real scroll arrived he judged it a forgery

artworld-02-c3.text: National Palace Museum (2020). The Epitome of Aesthetics: Digital Impressions. National Palace Museum, Taipei.
artworld-02-c3.quote: Following the research of modern scholars, including comparison of the quality of brush and ink in the two versions, it was confirmed that ''The Ziming Scroll'' is actually a copy.
artworld-02-c3.claim: Modern scholars, comparing the quality of brush and ink, have confirmed that the Ziming scroll is the copy.

artworld-03-c1.text: Los Angeles County Museum of Art. Islamic Art Collection at LACMA.
artworld-03-c1.quote: Contrary to a popular misconception, however, figural imagery is an important aspect of Islamic art.
artworld-03-c1.claim: As the Los Angeles County Museum of Art puts it, figural imagery is an important part of Islamic art.

artworld-03-c1.text: Los Angeles County Museum of Art. Islamic Art Collection at LACMA.
artworld-03-c1.quote: The Qur’an does not speak against the creation of figural images, only the making of idols.
artworld-03-c1.claim: The distinction matters: the Qur'an itself speaks against idols, not against images in general.

artworld-03-c1.text: Cleveland Museum of Art. Art of the Islamic World. Cleveland Museum of Art.
artworld-03-c1.quote: Interlocking human and animal forms in dynamic poses form the letters and accents in this unique style of calligraphy, the highest form of Islamic art.
artworld-03-c1.claim: Around its rim runs an inscription in animated script, in which the letters themselves are formed from human and animal bodies in lively poses.

artworld-03-c2.text: Los Angeles County Museum of Art. Islamic Art Collection at LACMA.
artworld-03-c2.quote: The names of certain calligraphers are well known, which is not surprising given the primacy of the written word in Islam
artworld-03-c2.claim: Most Islamic craftsmen are anonymous, but the names of many calligraphers were remembered.

artworld-03-c2.text: Los Angeles County Museum of Art. Islamic Art Collection at LACMA.
artworld-03-c2.quote: A few rare Qur'ans were produced on dyed parchment, and the museum’s collection includes a page from one of these sumptuous manuscripts, which was copied in gold Kufic on parchment dyed blue
artworld-03-c2.claim: A few luxurious copies were written in gold on parchment dyed deep blue

artworld-03-c2.text: Mohammad Ali Jalal Yaghan (2020). Mathematical concepts in Arabic calligraphy: The proportions of the ʾAlif. PLOS ONE.
artworld-03-c2.quote: Relating the components of the theory was, also, opened for opinions and interpretations, for example, the number of dots for the ʾAlif was never agreed upon.
artworld-03-c2.claim: A 2020 study of the historical texts notes that writers never agreed on how many dots tall the alif should be.

artworld-03-c3.text: Peter J. Lu, Paul J. Steinhardt (2007). Decagonal and quasi-crystalline tilings in medieval Islamic architecture. Science.
artworld-03-c3.quote: We show that by 1200 C.E. a conceptual breakthrough occurred in which girih patterns were reconceived as tessellations of a special set of equilateral polygons ("girih tiles") decorated with lines.
artworld-03-c3.claim: By about 1200, they argued, designers had begun to think of girih as tilings of a small set of shapes, from pentagons to bow-ties, each decorated with lines.

artworld-03-c3.text: Peter J. Lu, Paul J. Steinhardt (2007). Decagonal and quasi-crystalline tilings in medieval Islamic architecture. Science.
artworld-03-c3.quote: by the 15th century, the tessellation approach was combined with self-similar transformations to construct nearly perfect quasi-crystalline Penrose patterns, five centuries before their discovery in the West.
artworld-03-c3.claim: If they are right, Iranian craftsmen built a nearly perfect quasi-crystalline pattern five centuries before Western mathematics described one.

artworld-03-c3.text: Philip Ball (2007). Islamic tiles reveal sophisticated maths. Nature News.
artworld-03-c3.quote: Although they were probably unaware of the mathematical properties and consequences of the construction rule they devised, they did end up with something that would lead to what we understand today to be a quasi-crystal.
artworld-03-c3.claim: Lu himself thinks the designers were probably unaware of the mathematics; they wanted a pattern that could grow without repeating.

artworld-03-c3.text: Branko Grünbaum (2006). What symmetry groups are present in the Alhambra?. Notices of the AMS.
artworld-03-c3.quote: Groups of symmetry had no relevance to artists and artisans who decorated the Alhambra.
artworld-03-c3.claim: Groups of symmetry had no relevance to artists and artisans who decorated the Alhambra.

artworld-04-c1.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c1.quote: Slightly contradictory contemporary sources record that the tales filled 12 or 14 bound volumes, each with 100 paintings, and that the work took 15 years to complete.
artworld-04-c1.claim: Contemporary sources say the work filled 12 or 14 volumes of 100 paintings each and took 15 years

artworld-04-c1.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c1.quote: Some were rescued from the windows of the shop, where they had been used to block out the winter frosts of the previous season.
artworld-04-c1.claim: some of which had been used in the shop windows to keep out the winter frost

artworld-04-c2.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c2.quote: These inscriptions, written in red ink beneath each illustration, record that one designed the composition (tarh), while a second, presumably junior, artist was responsible for the 'work' (‘amal), filling in the colours of this outline.
artworld-04-c2.claim: and under each one a court librarian wrote in red ink who did what

artworld-04-c2.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c2.quote: The principles of scientific perspective were not followed, but a sense of depth derived from European art is found in some of the paintings in the Akbarnama.
artworld-04-c2.claim: Some Akbarnama scenes gain a sense of depth from European art, but the rules of scientific perspective were not followed.

artworld-04-c3.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c3.quote: on the right of the painting, the emperor himself has written in his distinctive spidery hand that it was the work of one his two leading artists, Mansur
artworld-04-c3.claim: The painting of it, now in the V&A, carries a note in Jahangir's own spidery handwriting

artworld-04-c3.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c3.quote: One of the leading court artists was ordered to make a copy of it, and when Roe was shown the original, accompanied by five identical versions, he had some difficulty in recognising his own.
artworld-04-c3.claim: when Roe was shown the original together with five identical versions, he had difficulty recognising his own

artworld-04-c3.text: Victoria and Albert Museum. The arts of the Mughal Empire. Victoria and Albert Museum.
artworld-04-c3.quote: Portraiture reached an unprecedented level of naturalism under Jahangir, a phenomenon that is usually attributed to the royal artists' exposure to European portraits.
artworld-04-c3.claim: The V&A notes that it is usually attributed to the artists' exposure to European portraits

artworld-05-c1.text: Weltmuseum Wien. The feather headdress. Weltmuseum Wien.
artworld-05-c1.quote: Although there once were many such feather headdresses from Mesoamerica, none of them, other than the one in Vienna, has survived.
artworld-05-c1.claim: This one, made in the early 16th century, is the only one left anywhere.

artworld-05-c1.text: Weltmuseum Wien. The feather headdress. Weltmuseum Wien.
artworld-05-c1.quote: Although lists of many of these objects have survived, the feather headdress cannot be identified among them.
artworld-05-c1.claim: many objects were shipped to Europe and listed, but this headdress cannot be identified in any of those lists

artworld-05-c1.text: Constanza Ontiveros (2026). Austrian presidential hopeful pledges to return Moctezuma’s headdress to Mexico. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-05-c1.quote: “The headdress’s origin is uncertain, and its association with Moctezuma came much later,” the Mexican historian Federico Navarrete tells The Art Newspaper.
artworld-05-c1.claim: the Mexican historian Federico Navarrete says its association with Moctezuma came much later

artworld-05-c2.text: Constanza Ontiveros (2026). Austrian presidential hopeful pledges to return Moctezuma’s headdress to Mexico. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-05-c2.quote: Austria cites the headdress's fragility as the reason for rejecting its loan.
artworld-05-c2.claim: Austria said no, citing the object's fragility

artworld-05-c2.text: Weltmuseum Wien. The feather headdress. Weltmuseum Wien.
artworld-05-c2.quote: At least 170 breaks were detected in the headdress’s 374 long quetzal feathers.
artworld-05-c2.claim: They found at least 170 breaks in its 374 long quetzal feathers

artworld-05-c2.text: Weltmuseum Wien. The feather headdress. Weltmuseum Wien.
artworld-05-c2.quote: He determined that it was practically impossible to move the headdress using the standard modes of transportation for international loans (motor vehicles and airplanes) without risking damage.
artworld-05-c2.claim: His conclusion: it was practically impossible to move it by lorry or aircraft, the standard ways of moving loans, without risking damage.

artworld-05-c3.text: Dumbarton Oaks. Early Byzantine Furnishing Textiles and Pre-Columbian Dress. Dumbarton Oaks.
artworld-05-c3.quote: Textiles, more than gold and precious stones, marked a person’s social status in the ancient Andes.
artworld-05-c3.claim: textiles, more than gold and precious stones, marked a person's social status

artworld-05-c3.text: Encyclopedia.com. Textiles, Andean. Encyclopedia of Clothing and Fashion (Encyclopedia.com).
artworld-05-c3.quote: Finely spun and brightly colored cloth reserved for the Inca nobility was called silk by the Spanish because such smooth, lustrous, and fine-to-the-touch fabric was only known in Europe from Chinese cloth.
artworld-05-c3.claim: The smoothest royal cloth felt so fine that the Spanish called it silk, a fabric Europe knew only from Chinese cloth.

artworld-05-c3.text: Encyclopedia.com. Textiles, Andean. Encyclopedia of Clothing and Fashion (Encyclopedia.com).
artworld-05-c3.quote: They worked on an unusual frame loom at least twice as wide as it was tall.
artworld-05-c3.claim: Qompi was woven on an unusual frame loom at least twice as wide as it was tall.

artworld-05-c3.text: Encyclopedia.com. Textiles, Andean. Encyclopedia of Clothing and Fashion (Encyclopedia.com).
artworld-05-c3.quote: Large checkerboard patterns and other repeating designs indicated social or military roles, while more elaborate registered patterns called tokapu may have functioned within a still obscure system of communication.
artworld-05-c3.claim: Others suggest the registered patterns may have worked as a still obscure system of communication

artworld-06-c1.text: Damien Finch, Andrew Gleadow (2021). This 17,500-year-old kangaroo in the Kimberley is Australia’s oldest Aboriginal rock painting. The Conversation.
artworld-06-c1.quote: Unfortunately, no current scientific dating method can determine when this paint was applied to the rock surface.
artworld-06-c1.claim: no current scientific method can tell when such paint was put on the rock

artworld-06-c1.text: Damien Finch, Andrew Gleadow (2021). This 17,500-year-old kangaroo in the Kimberley is Australia’s oldest Aboriginal rock painting. The Conversation.
artworld-06-c1.quote: With these ages, we determined confidently the painting is between 17,500 and 17,100 years old; most likely close to 17,300 years old.
artworld-06-c1.claim: Three nests lay beneath it and three on top, which pinned its age to between 17,500 and 17,100 years, most likely about 17,300.

artworld-06-c1.text: Damien Finch, Andrew Gleadow, Janet Hergt, Pauline Heaney, Helen Green, et al (2021). Ages for Australia’s oldest rock paintings. Nature Human Behaviour.
artworld-06-c1.quote: At the request of Balanggarra Aboriginal Traditional Owners of the land where the samples were collected, the data do not include exact locations of rock art sites.
artworld-06-c1.claim: the published data do not give the exact locations of the sites

artworld-06-c2.text: National Gallery of Victoria. Tjukurrtjanu: Origins of Western Desert Art. National Gallery of Victoria.
artworld-06-c2.quote: the ancient visual language of the Western Desert was rendered permanent on sheets of composition board and thereby transformed into a rich new art form: artefact became art.
artworld-06-c2.claim: As the National Gallery of Victoria puts it, artefact became art.

artworld-06-c2.text: John Kean (2017). Friday essay: how the Men’s Painting Room at Papunya transformed Australian art. The Conversation.
artworld-06-c2.quote: Not only did Kaapa receive the prize but all seven of the works Cooke had delivered to Alice Springs sold, returning around $750 to the artist.
artworld-06-c2.claim: and all seven works sold, earning him about $750 and causing a sensation back home

artworld-06-c2.text: Drill Hall Gallery, Australian National University. Pintupi Way Review. Drill Hall Gallery (ANU).
artworld-06-c2.quote: painting was dynamic before Bardon even arrived in Papunya and that the Warlpiri Men’s Museum in Yundumu had opened before the school mural was ever mentioned
artworld-06-c2.claim: A reviewer citing the curator Luke Scholes argues that painting was already dynamic before Bardon arrived

artworld-06-c2.text: Matthew Rimmer (2007). A right of resale? Indigenous art under the hammer. ABC News.
artworld-06-c2.quote: The significant art work was bought by the Commonwealth Bank for a mere $1,200 in 1977, and spent 20 years hanging in the canteen of the bank's Mornington Peninsula training centre.
artworld-06-c2.claim: The Commonwealth Bank bought it that year for $1,200 and hung it in a staff training centre canteen for some 20 years.

artworld-06-c3.text: Tynan King (2024). ‘We didn’t have dots’: How Aboriginal visual language became homogenised. ABC News.
artworld-06-c3.quote: “We didn’t have dots, we had lines,” he explains, gesturing at the 30-metre mural in Parramatta Square.
artworld-06-c3.claim: We didn't have dots, we had lines.

artworld-06-c3.text: National Gallery of Victoria. A bold aesthetic: the Lajamanu panels. National Gallery of Victoria.
artworld-06-c3.quote: Part of their reticence may have stemmed from the controversy at Papunya in 1972–73 when founding artists inadvertently included depictions of sacred objects (tjurunga) and ritual head ornaments (wanigi) in works brought into Alice Springs for sale.
artworld-06-c3.claim: In 1972–73 controversy erupted because founding artists had inadvertently included depictions of sacred objects

artworld-06-c3.text: Tynan King (2024). ‘We didn’t have dots’: How Aboriginal visual language became homogenised. ABC News.
artworld-06-c3.quote: as the paintings became more popular and travelled further afield, dots were used more frequently to obscure sacred and dangerous symbology
artworld-06-c3.claim: dots were used more often to obscure sacred and dangerous symbols

artworld-06-c3.text: National Gallery of Victoria. Tjukurrtjanu: Origins of Western Desert Art. National Gallery of Victoria.
artworld-06-c3.quote: following a comprehensive consultation process, these works will be exhibited separately for the duration of the exhibition and will not be illustrated in the exhibition catalogue or displayed on this website.
artworld-06-c3.claim: culturally sensitive works were hung separately after consultation and left out of the catalogue and website

artworld-07-c1.text: Gareth Harris (2026). Cambridge University to return 100 Benin Bronzes to Nigeria. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-07-c1.quote: ('Benin bronzes' refers to objects made of brass and ivory as well as bronze)
artworld-07-c1.claim: Many treasures in the group are carved ivory, not metal at all.

artworld-07-c1.text: Tobias B. Skowronek, Christopher R. DeCorse, Rolf Denk, et al (2023). German brass for Benin Bronzes: Geochemical analysis insights into the early Atlantic trade. PLOS ONE.
artworld-07-c1.quote: indicate that the majority are either brass or leaded brass, sometimes with small amounts of tin
artworld-07-c1.claim: And the metal ones are mostly not bronze.

artworld-07-c1.text: Cleveland Museum of Art. Plaque (1953.425). Cleveland Museum of Art.
artworld-07-c1.quote: The bent sides of this plaque once helped attach it to wooden beams in a palace.
artworld-07-c1.claim: the bent sides of one in the Cleveland Museum of Art show how it was fixed to wooden beams

artworld-07-c1.text: Pitt Rivers Museum. The Kingdom of Benin. Pitt Rivers Museum, University of Oxford.
artworld-07-c1.quote: Iy’Ọba was a title first given to Queen Idia, the mother of Ọba Ẹsigie, in the late 1400s.
artworld-07-c1.claim: The title of Iyoba was first given in the late 1400s to

artworld-07-c2.text: Tobias B. Skowronek, Christopher R. DeCorse, Rolf Denk, et al (2023). German brass for Benin Bronzes: Geochemical analysis insights into the early Atlantic trade. PLOS ONE.
artworld-07-c2.quote: Out of the 212 Benin Bronzes that were analysed 113 fall into what the authors describe as “unusually small field”
artworld-07-c2.claim: Earlier work had found Benin Bronzes oddly uniform: of 212 analysed, 113 fall into an unusually small field of ratios.

artworld-07-c2.text: Tobias B. Skowronek, Christopher R. DeCorse, Rolf Denk, et al (2023). German brass for Benin Bronzes: Geochemical analysis insights into the early Atlantic trade. PLOS ONE.
artworld-07-c2.quote: Manillas from the 18th century onwards can be related to some of the Benin Bronzes but do not fit to the bulk cluster of the famous artworks.
artworld-07-c2.claim: Later manillas matched only some of the bronzes.

artworld-07-c2.text: Tobias B. Skowronek, Christopher R. DeCorse, Rolf Denk, et al (2023). German brass for Benin Bronzes: Geochemical analysis insights into the early Atlantic trade. PLOS ONE.
artworld-07-c2.quote: However, the difference in trace elemental patterns between manillas and Benin Bronzes does not allow postulating that they have been the only source.
artworld-07-c2.claim: while noting that differences in trace elements mean they may not have been the only one

artworld-07-c2.text: Cleveland Museum of Art. Art from the Benin Kingdom. Cleveland Museum of Art.
artworld-07-c2.quote: Benin gained brass through trade: European currency rings (manillas) were exchanged for people that Ẹdo enslaved in wars.
artworld-07-c2.claim: As the Cleveland Museum of Art states, European manillas were exchanged for people whom the Edo had enslaved in wars.

artworld-07-c2.text: Cleveland Museum of Art. Plaque (1953.425). Cleveland Museum of Art.
artworld-07-c2.quote: Recently, an art historian virtually reconstructed their former display in the palace based on their dimensions and imagery.
artworld-07-c2.claim: An art historian has since reconstructed their former arrangement on the palace walls virtually, working from their dimensions and their imagery.

artworld-07-c3.text: Gareth Harris (2022). ‘The Benin Bronzes are returning home’: Germany and Nigeria sign historic restitution agreement. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-07-c3.quote: The British Museum is prohibited from permanently removing items from its collection under a 1963 UK law.
artworld-07-c3.claim: The British Museum holds around 900 and is barred by a 1963 UK law from permanently removing items from its collection.

artworld-07-c3.text: Horniman Museum and Gardens (2024). New Benin display at the Horniman includes returned bronzes on loan. Horniman Museum and Gardens.
artworld-07-c3.quote: Of the 72 objects, six were physically returned to Nigeria in 2022, with the rest remaining at the Horniman under a loan agreement.
artworld-07-c3.claim: transferred ownership of 72 objects in November 2022, sent six back and keeps the rest on loan

artworld-07-c3.text: Gareth Harris (2023). Nigeria transfers ownership of Benin Bronzes to royal ruler. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-07-c3.quote: The Benin Bronzes restitution saga has taken a new turn after the Nigerian government has officially recognised the Oba of Benin (Oba Ewuare II) as the owner and custodian of the artefacts looted in the late 19th century.
artworld-07-c3.claim: In March 2023 a presidential declaration recognised the Oba, Ewuare II, as owner and custodian of the returned artefacts.

artworld-07-c3.text: Benjamin Sutton (2024). US Supreme Court declines to hear case challenging Smithsonian's restitution of Benin Bronzes. The Art Newspaper.
artworld-07-c3.quote: The justices of the Supreme Court of the United States have opted not to hear a case that sought to block the Smithsonian Institution from returning 29 Benin Bronzes from its collection to Nigeria.
artworld-07-c3.claim: It lost, and the US Supreme Court declined to hear the case in 2024.
